method.abandon_rule: a sweep stops climbing once a rung exceeds 266 ms at p50 or takes over 8 s to build; the rungs above are reported unmeasured with the reason
method.attempts: a configuration whose frames were not drawn is re-measured up to 3 times before being recorded as unmeasured
method.camera: directly overhead at the altitude where the footprint fills the frame vertically, 60° vertical FOV. Every instance is in frustum.
method.draw_calls: Performance's per-frame draw-call count, so a flat frame time can be told from instances that stopped being drawn
method.frame_ms: elapsed time between frames, vsync disabled and no fps cap
method.gpu_ms: RenderingServer's own measured viewport render time, where the renderer implements it; absent with a reason where it does not
method.placement: uniform random in the square, seed 20260903
method.primitives: Performance's per-frame primitive count: instances x triangles if everything in the footprint is really being rendered
method.quantiles: nearest-rank: p99 of 80 frames is the 80th-ranked frame, not an interpolation
method.self_check: every configuration's primitive count is compared with instances x triangles, and its draw calls with what the technique needs. A rung whose frames did not draw what was asked is marked unmeasured with the counts, rather than contributing a frame time to the fit.
method.wall_clock_mean_ms: total elapsed time over the frames counted, as a second reading of the same frames: the per-frame delta quantises on this platform and a mean that disagrees with p50 is how that shows
method.window: always on top and moved to the foreground. An unfocused window on some platforms stops being drawn while the main loop keeps ticking, which yields a full set of frame times off a fixed cadence

not_here.culling: every instance is in frustum by construction. A real view culls, so these are the costs of a cell wholly in view.
not_here.other_hardware: the coefficient is per machine and per renderer. Nothing here extrapolates to another GPU, and the numbers should be re-measured rather than scaled.
not_here.shading: one unshaded-complexity opaque material, no shadows, no transparency, no LOD. M5's archetypes will differ and this is the floor rather than the estimate.
not_here.terrain: no basin is drawn. This measures instancing alone; a scene with M1's terrain under it would measure two things at once.

_vertical_exaggeration_note: 1.0, and added by hand rather than re-measured. This benchmark draws no terrain and no plants -- a placeholder mesh over a flat square, as its README says -- so its metres are true metres and there is nothing exaggerated to record. The field is here because the rule that every measurement states the exaggeration its distances were taken at is worth more without an exemption than with one: this artefact's coefficients are quoted into a scene drawn at 12x, and a reader comparing its 4 m instance height against a 52 m drawn tree needs to be told which is which. Nothing else in the file was touched; `tools/run_benchmark.sh` now emits it.
